thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary anomaly detected for model-runner-prod-canary. p95 latency >1300ms and throughput -42% vs baseline for the last 3m. Error rate up (5xx ~0.8%). Severity: SEV2. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/d/alerts/2087654321

Alex Chen: I'm oncall, digging in. Observability links?

Alex Chen: dashboards show spike at 08:10 UTC coinciding with rollout event.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-14T08:09:27Z — rollout id r-20260314-08-09 — version: model-runtime@v12.3.4 — feature flag toggled: dynamic_batching_v2 = true — target: prod-canary (20% traffic)

Priya Rao: tagging in. Looking at canary hosts now. 

Mateo Alvarez: I see repeated kernel fallback on canary nodes: 
```
[2026-03-14T08:10:31Z] kernel_fallback: true - reason: missing_fp16_kernels
[2026-03-14T08:10:31Z] batch_coalescer: queue_depth=1234 max_batch_tokens=4096 latency_ms=1300
[2026-03-14T08:10:34Z] fallback_kernel_exec: slow_path exec_count=987
```

Pablo (oncall-sre): queue depth is through the roof, batching degen. Looks like dynamic_batching_v2 reduced batch alignment, increasing head-of-line blocking. Kernel fallback cause: new kernel selection logic picking asm kernels that aren't optimized on this AMI.

Alex Chen: So likely combo: rollout toggled new batching, which triggers different kernel paths => fallback => slower per-token exec => lower throughput. Confirmed across 3 canary hosts.

Priya Rao: Confirmed impact: canary p95 up, canary throughput -40%, some requests getting 504s from request queue timeouts. Customer-facing traffic ~5% of those hits routed through canary (internal metric). Lia, FYI for customer ops.

Lia (customer-ops): copying. Will prepare templated note if rollback is needed. Which customers are impacted?

Alex Chen: early estimate: ~0.12% of total production requests affected; primarily internal staging and small set of PLG traffic. No major enterprise customers reported yet.

Kara (eng-manager): prioritize kill-switch + rollback plan. Keep customer comms ready.

Mateo Alvarez: quick mitigation tests: we can 1) flip dynamic_batching_v2 -> false (feature flag kill-switch), 2) rollback runtime to v12.3.3, or 3) patch kernel selection config to prefer stable kernels. Which do we flip first?

Pablo (oncall-sre): flip kill-switch first (low blast radius) — that'll revert batching code paths immediately without full rollback. If that doesn't bring latency down in 2 minutes, we rollback.

Alex Chen: Agreed. I'm flipping flag now: `curl -XPOST https://ff.redwood/api/flags/dynamic_batching_v2/off -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'`

deploy-gateway-bot: Feature flag dynamic_batching_v2 set to OFF by Alex Chen at 08:12:05 UTC (propagating)

Mateo Alvarez: metrics: 08:12:30 p95 dropped from 1350ms -> 720ms, throughput recovered ~+18% so partial improvement. Queue depth down to ~400. Good sign.

Priya Rao: but some kernels still fallback on existing workers, likely need pod restart to pick up kernel blacklist. I'm initiating rolling restart of canary pods (graceful): `kubectl rollout restart deploy/model-runner-canary --namespace=prod-canary`

Pablo (oncall-sre): restart started at 08:13:40 UTC. Monitoring.

Alex Chen: After restarts (08:14:50) p95 now ~520ms, throughput ~+35% vs trough, error rate back to baseline. Looks like kill-switch + restart mitigated.

Lia (customer-ops): drafting message: "We observed increased latency for a subset of requests during a canary rollout; mitigations applied and service restored. No action needed from customers." Will wait for final confirmation before sending.

Kara (eng-manager): Great. We still need root cause: why did dynamic_batching_v2 select kernels that don't exist on our AMI? Is it an infra mismatch or a code bug?

Mateo Alvarez: initial root cause hypothesis: v12.3.4 introduced a kernel selector that prefers new AVX512/asm kernels when batching changes produce wider token windows. The canary hosts in prod are on a slightly older AMI missing those asm kernels, causing fallback to slower interpreter path. On dedicated clusters (newer AMI) this would not have been seen.

Alex Chen: Action items: 
- (Alex) reopen a blocking rollout hold for v12.3.4 globally.
- (Mateo) add safeguard in kernel selector: verify kernel availability before switching (hotfix).
- (Pablo) add canary host AMI check as preflight for future rollout gating.
- (Priya) run synthetic load tests in staging with dynamic_batching_v2 enabled + old AMI to reproduce.
- (Lia) prepare postmortem customer note if any customers ask.

Priya Rao: setting rollout hold now: `deploy-bot hold r-20260314-08-09`

deploy-bot: Rollout r-20260314-08-09 marked HOLD by Priya Rao at 08:18:02 UTC — no further traffic will be increased.

Kara (eng-manager): Handoff: I'll take this through postmortem. Alex/Pablo, please coordinate with infra to identify all AMI variants. Priya/Mateo, prioritize the hotfix. Lia, hold on external comms until we have RCA.

Alex Chen: Handoff to night oncall (Priya) scheduled at 09:00 UTC. I'll update pager duty with incident summary.

incident-bot: Incident SEV2 auto-ack at 08:19:10 UTC — assigned to Alex Chen and Priya Rao.

Mateo Alvarez: quick repro note for postmortem: include logs snippet and `kernel_selector` config. Also capture `max_batch_tokens` distributions across requests.

Pablo (oncall-sre): monitoring alerts cleared at 08:21:30 UTC. Will keep a 2hr watch window. 

Lia (customer-ops): I'll queue a status update for internal stakeholders and draft a customer-safe blurb in case we need it later.

Alex Chen: summary: cause = new batching + kernel selector mismatch with older AMI -> kernel fallback -> batching degen -> latency/throughput regression. Mitigation = feature flag off + rolling pod restarts + rollout hold. Next: hotfix kernel availability checks + rollout gating by AMI.

Kara (eng-manager): Thanks team. Please add timeline entries and notes to the incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood/2087654321. We'll run RCA tomorrow.
